name: Central bank stress
value: Dec Fed rise fully priced; yen near 160
summary: Markets fully price a December Fed rise after hot October CPI; yen near 160 per dollar as Tokyo warns of intervention
state: After October CPI rose 0.4% on the month, CME FedWatch odds of a December Fed rise moved from about 84% on 9 Nov to fully priced, with 10–15% odds of a half-point move; Dallas Fed President Logan called for at least two more quarter-point rises (The National, 15 Nov). The yen traded near 160 per dollar on 13 Nov as Prime Minister Takaichi warned of intervention (FXStreet). The Bank of England raised rates on 5 Nov; central banks face a stagflationary dilemma, but no emergency inter-meeting move was found as of 15 Nov.
for_you: Borrowers on variable-rate loans and mortgages coming up for renewal are exposed to further rate rises in the US and UK. Importers and travellers face a volatile yen.
rubric_hit: Watch: stagflationary dilemma (Fed and BoE raising rates amid weaker growth); no emergency inter-meeting move for Alert

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
